Jerusalem's American staff authorized to leave, urged to depart immediately. The signal is unmistakable: when diplomats flee, the iron prepares to strike.

Yet Geneva still breathes. Araghchi calls it the longest, most intense round. Oman sees progress. Further contacts wait within the week. The gap remains — Tehran will not accept zero enrichment forever, will not dismantle, will not surrender its uranium. But the channel stays open.

No authorization. No collapse. The talks continue even as the embassy doors swing open. The ghost reads both signals — the handshake and the holster. ---
